_comment: Guided tour for HydroPro. Steps point at real controls and wait for the user to press them. Read by chisurf.gui.widgets.tools.guided_tour.

steps.title: What this tool computes
steps.text:
HydroPro predicts the translational diffusion coefficient of a rigid protein from its PDB file, with the external HYDROPRO program. The same run writes the rotational relaxation times you compare with an anisotropy decay.

HYDROPRO is downloaded separately; it is not part of ChiSurf.

steps.title: Start with a sphere you know
steps.text: Load example builds a sphere of radius 17 Å from atoms on a lattice and points the tool at a stand-in solver that applies only the Stokes–Einstein law, D = kBT/(6πηR). The answer is known: 1.19×10⁻⁶ cm²/s at 20 °C in water. The stand-in is not HYDROPRO; for real structures download the program.

steps.title: Point at the program
steps.text: With your own data, choose the HYDROPRO 10 binary here. Its file name must contain hydropro: any other name is treated as HYDRO++, and then the settings in this form are not used. The example has filled this in.

steps.title: Choose the structures
steps.text: One job per PDB file. Remove crystal waters, ligands and alternate conformations first: every non-hydrogen atom except water oxygens becomes part of the body.

steps.title: INDMODE and AER go together
steps.text: Mode 1 (atomic, shell) with AER = 2.9 Å is the reference. Mode 2 needs 4.8 Å and mode 4 needs 6.1 Å. AER contains the hydration layer and is calibrated — keep it at these values.

steps.title: Temperature and viscosity set the answer
steps.text: Every diffusion coefficient scales as T/η. ETA is in poise: water at 20 °C is 0.01 P. Enter your buffer's viscosity if it is not water.

steps.title: Mass only matters for sedimentation
steps.text: RM, VBAR and RHO enter the sedimentation coefficient and intrinsic viscosity, not the diffusion coefficient. Replace the 100 000 Da placeholder with the real mass if you want those.

steps.title: Run
steps.text: The jobs run off the GUI thread; an output window shows the program's console. Each structure gets a folder under ~/.hydropp_gui.

steps.title: Read the table, then the report
steps.text: The table shows Dt in cm²/s. The rotational relaxation times are in <name>-res.txt in the job folder. Save CSV writes the table; copy reports you want to keep, because the next run overwrites them.
